findings.description: POST /api/admin/disputes/{id}/resolve and /dismiss are guarded by HAS_ADMIN_ROLE, which is "hasRole('ROLE_ADMIN') or hasRole('ROLE_LTD_ADMIN')". DisputeService.resolveDispute moves real money: FULL_CREDIT/PARTIAL_CREDIT write wallet DISPUTE_CREDIT entries, UPHOLD_COACH claws back the payer's refund and enqueues Stripe payout top-ups, and every resolution cuts, reverses or releases the coach payout. A ROLE_LTD_ADMIN account — defined as a limited reads-and-moderation tier — can therefore credit a colluding parent the full session price or pay a colluding coach in full. No full-admin-only expression exists anywhere in SecurityConstants, and no other filter restricts LTD_ADMIN writes.
findings.title: Dispute resolve/dismiss admit ROLE_LTD_ADMIN, letting the read-only admin tier move money
findings.verification: Confirm with the owners that ROLE_LTD_ADMIN is intended to be reads/moderation only (as the role model states); grep confirms SecurityConstants has no HAS_FULL_ADMIN_ROLE and no code path anywhere distinguishes ROLE_ADMIN from ROLE_LTD_ADMIN for write actions.

findings.description: POST /api/admin/bookings/{id}/force-complete uses HAS_ADMIN_ROLE, so a ROLE_LTD_ADMIN account can force-complete any COMPLETED_PENDING_CONFIRMATION booking. forceCompleteWithPlaceholderData publishes BookingCompletedEvent, and CoachPayoutEnqueueListener enqueues the coach payout BEFORE_COMMIT — money movement for a session nobody confirmed, triggered by the tier that is supposed to be read/moderation only. Impact is bounded because StuckCompletionSweeperService would eventually force-complete the same bookings, but the limited admin chooses the timing and target.
findings.title: Admin force-complete admits ROLE_LTD_ADMIN and releases the coach payout
findings.verification: Same role-model confirmation as the dispute-resolve finding; verify StuckCompletionSweeperService's own selection criteria match what the admin endpoint can reach.

findings.description: The H1 fix derives the wrap-up mode server-side so a quick-complete cannot claim LIVE, but LIVE only requires that the coach pressed Start (allowed the moment requestedStartTime passes) and ended the session themselves — with no minimum elapsed time. A coach who never coaches can press Start, immediately call endSession, and submit the wrap-up: the server derives LIVE, the booking goes COMPLETED and the payout is enqueued at once, with no parent confirmation window. This reproduces the exact outcome the fix removed for quick-complete (completion and payment for a session that never happened), leaving the parent only the reactive 14-day dispute path against the 48h payout hold.
findings.symbol: submitWrapUp (mode derivation: liveStartedAt != null && autoEndedAt == null)
findings.title: Coach can bypass the parent-confirmation window by pressing Start then End back-to-back
findings.verification: Confirm there is no other guard (e.g., minimum session duration or end-time check) between START and COMPLETE_PENDING; BookingStateMachine and endSession show none.

findings.description: bookingQuickCompleteConfirm.html tells the parent to "confirm or dispute this session" within 24 hours, and BookingStateMachine models DISPUTE from COMPLETED_PENDING_CONFIRMATION — but raiseDispute lists that status in neither ELIGIBLE_STATUSES nor LIVE_STATUSES, so a dispute attempt during the confirmation window fails with NOT_ELIGIBLE. A parent who follows the email, is refused, and gives up has the session auto-confirmed by QuickCompleteTimeoutService and the coach paid; contesting requires knowing to return after completion and dispute within the 48h payout hold.
findings.title: Parent told to 'confirm or dispute' a quick-complete cannot actually raise a dispute during the window
findings.verification: Confirm the frontend dispute entry point is also status-gated the same way; the backend refusal is verifiable directly from the status lists.

findings.description: raiseDispute reads the booking without a row lock, so a parent disputing an IN_PROGRESS/PAUSED session can race the coach's LIVE submitWrapUp commit: the dispute transaction sees the pre-commit live status and finds no coach_payouts row (freezeForDispute is a no-op), while the completion transaction's enqueuePayout checks existsOpenDisputeForBooking before the dispute commits and creates the payout PENDING_RELEASE with a transfer enqueued. CoachPayoutTransferHandler re-checks only the row's own freeze flags and the safety hold at release time — not open disputes — so after the 48h hold the transfer goes to the coach with the dispute still open, degrading recovery to a Stripe reversal that can fail (REVERSAL_FAILED coach debt).
findings.title: Dispute raised concurrently with session completion leaves the payout unfrozen and it releases while the dispute is open
findings.verification: Confirm no serialization exists between the two paths (raiseDispute takes neither the booking row lock nor any advisory lock); confirmed CoachPayoutTransferHandler lines 75-116 re-check flags and safety hold only.

findings.description: dispute.setCreditAmount(creditAmount) records the request value verbatim: a NO_ACTION resolution submitted with a stray creditAmount records a credit that was never issued, and a FULL_CREDIT records null while the computed remainder was actually credited. The admin dispute detail (AdminDisputeDetailDto.creditAmount) and the wallet ledger then disagree, so the audit record of a money-moving action is wrong; the raiser's notification uses the correct 'credited' value, masking the skew.
findings.title: resolveDispute stores the submitted creditAmount, not what was actually credited
findings.verification: Trigger by POSTing resolve with resolution=NO_ACTION and creditAmount=100, then fetch the admin dispute detail and compare with the parent_credit_ledger rows for the booking.
